title: Oily Steamy Norwegian Kasha Pilaf
description: A hearty, one-pot dish from Norway featuring dark brown sugar and a unique steamy cooking process.
instructions: Combine kasha, dark brown sugar, grainy mustard, salt, and black pepper in a kazan cauldron or large pot with a lid.
Add water to the pot, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the kasha is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Add butter to the pot and stir until melted.
Increase heat to high and cover the pot for 5 minutes, creating a steamy environment.
Remove the pot from the heat and let cool slightly, then fluff the pilaf with a fork.
Stir in chopped fresh dill and serve hot.
Be careful when removing the pot from the heat as it may be hot and steamy.
Let the pilaf rest for a few minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
If desired, serve with additional chopped fresh dill on top.
This dish is best served hot, straight from the pot.
Note that the steamy cooking process is an important part of this recipe, so be sure to cover the pot and cook over high heat for the last 5 minutes.
The kasha will absorb the flavors and the dark brown sugar will caramelize, creating a rich and satisfying pilaf.
